channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Federal Reserve Chair Warsh: Inflation trends were not passing the test
item.description: Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair Kevin Warsh is holding a press conference following the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) decision to raise the Funds Target Range to 3.75%–4.00%, as expected.

item.title: Fed raises 2026 interest rate forecast to 4.1%, lifts PCE inflation projections
item.description: The Federal Reserve's (Fed) latest dot plot projections, released by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) on Wednesday, show policymakers now expect interest rates to stand at 4.1% by the end of 2026, up from 3.8% in June.

item.title: Australian Dollar slides below 0.7100 as Warsh strikes hawkish tone
item.description: AUD/USD extends losses on Wednesday after the Federal Reserve (Fed) raised interest rates and released a hawkish set of policy projections. The pair slides more than 20 pips in the immediate reaction and trades around 0.7093 at the time of writing.

item.title: Fed’s Warsh: Decision today was the right decision
item.description: This section below was published at 18:00 GMT to cover the Federal Reserve's policy decisions and the immediate market reaction.

item.title: The Fed hikes six days after the ECB, weighing on the Euro
item.description: The European Central Bank (ECB) moved first. Six days ago it raised its deposit rate, the return banks earn on money parked with it, by a quarter-point to 2.50%. The Fed matched that size on Wednesday and went to 3.75-4.00%, its first increase since 2023.

item.title: A Fed rate hike sends the Loonie to a six-week low
item.description: The Bank of Canada has held its overnight rate at 2.25% through seven consecutive meetings, the most recent on September 2, and does not decide again until October 28. The Fed ended a pause of its own on Wednesday, lifting its rate to 3.75-4.00%.

item.title: WTI holds near daily low as Fed decision draws muted reaction
item.description: Texas Intermediate (WTI) Oil holds near its daily low on Wednesday, showing little immediate reaction to the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) monetary policy announcement. At the time of writing, WTI trades around $97.50 per barrel, down roughly 3.3% on the day.

item.title: The Federal Reserve hikes back above Britain's cash rate
item.description: The Fed has raised its rate to 3.75-4.00%, its first increase since 2023 and its first move since the cut in December 2025. Bank Rate, the Bank of England's own rate, has been 3.75% since December 2025.

item.title: Japanese Yen falls as US Federal Reserve delivers
item.description: The USD/JPY pair trades at fresh weekly highs in the 155.50 price zone after the United States (US) Federal Reserve (Fed) delivered the expected 25 basis point (bps) interest rate hike. The US Dollar (USD) resumed its weekly advance with the headlines, following a pause ahead of the announcement.

item.title: Dollar Index Cracks 100 as Fed delivers hawkish hike
item.description: The Fed has raised its rate to 3.75-4.00%, its first increase since 2023. This index measures the Dollar against six currencies, and it is not a broad measure. The Euro alone is 57.6% of it.

item.title: The Dow Jones' 30 corporate borrowers eat a Fed rate hike
item.description: The Fed has raised its rate to 3.75-4.00%, its first increase since 2023 and its first move of any kind since the cut in December 2025. The rate it sets is what banks pay to borrow from each other overnight, and it reaches this index in two places.

item.title: Federal Reserve hawkish hike sent Gold price lower
item.description: The United States (US) Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) announced a 25 basis-point (bps) interest rate hike following its two-day meeting, pushing the US Dollar (USD) firmly up against most major rivals. With this decision, the Funds Target Range (FFTR) stands floating in the 3.75%–4.00% range.

item.title: The Fed hikes to 4% as the 10-year yield toys with 5%
item.description: The Fed has raised its rate to 3.75-4.00%, its first increase since 2023 and its first move since the cut in December 2025. The rate it controls is the overnight one. Everything further out is set by people buying and selling bonds, and they have been selling.

item.title: WTI pulls back below $100 as Saudi Arabia steps up efforts to restore Oil flows
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Oil falls on Wednesday as Saudi Arabia steps up efforts to restore flows through its East-West pipeline, which was damaged by a drone attack last week.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar steadies as markets await Fed decision
item.description: NZD/USD trades around 0.5755 at the time of writing on Wednesday, virtually unchanged on the day after rebounding from an over two-month low at 0.5737.

item.title: Gold consolidates gains as traders brace for Fed interest rate decision
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) consolidates gains on Wednesday after rebounding during Asian trading hours, supported by a modest pullback in Oil prices and US Treasury yields.

item.title: The Pound sells its own inflation spike ahead of a Fed hike
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) trades just above 1.3450 on Wednesday, down 23 pips, after a morning that ran in two directions. It climbed into the August inflation release at 06:00 GMT, spiked on it, then spent six hours handing the move back and another 30 pips with it.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average huddles ahead of Fed action
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average trades just above 52,100 and has spent the Wednesday morning going nowhere, on the day the Federal Reserve (Fed) is expected to raise its rate for the first time since 2023. That is not indifference.

item.title: Euro: Consolidation with downside risks against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note the Euro (EUR) is consolidating in a tight range around the mid-1.15s as markets await the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC).

item.title: US Dollar: Fed repricing risk caps downside – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley notes the US Dollar (USD) has outperformed G10 peers on expectations the Fed will deliver around 100 bps of tightening over 12 months, but warns this may be excessive.

item.title: British Pound: BoE repricing risk grows – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes GBP/USD is trading heavy near its 200-day moving average as United Kingdom (UK) gilts stabilize. August Consumer Price Index (CPI) slightly exceeded the Bank of England's (BoE) projections, but he still expects the BoE to hold rates at 3.75%.

item.title: Australian Dollar holds ground as Fed decision looms
item.description: AUD/USD trades in a narrow range on Wednesday as investors hold back from taking strong positions ahead of the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) monetary policy announcement. At the time of writing, AUD/USD trades around 0.7134, little changed on the day.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: BoC hawkish tilt and key levels – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret report USD/CAD is steady near 1.39 as markets await the Federal Reserve (Fed) and the Bank of Canada’s (BoC) summary of deliberations. They note the BoC is likely to sound more hawkish after firmer inflation data and still-accommodative policy.

item.title: United Kingdom: BoE hold view reinforced – Nomura
item.description: Nomura’s Global Markets Research team, including Josie Anderson, George Buckley and Andrzej Szczepaniak, notes that UK CPI data for August came in broadly as expected, with headline inflation at 3.1% and core and services measures unchanged.

item.title: Eurozone: Manufacturing outlook steadies as year-end hopes build – ING
item.description: ING’s Bert Colijn notes that Eurozone industrial production slipped by 0.1% in both June and July, leaving output broadly unchanged from a year earlier. He highlights resilience in capital goods and energy, but continued weakness in consumer-focused sectors, especially non-durable goods.

item.title: Euro trades cautiously against US Dollar ahead of expected Fed rate hike
item.description: EUR/USD consolidates losses on Wednesday as traders avoid taking strong directional positions ahead of the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) monetary policy announcement.

item.title: Silver price rebounds ahead of expected Fed rate hike, Warsh press conference
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) rebounds on Wednesday and trades around $64.00 per troy ounce at the time of writing, up 1.32% on the day.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed pricing creates asymmetric risks – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad says the US Dollar (USD) remains supported by energy-driven risk aversion ahead of the FOMC decision.

item.title: Bank of England: Hawkish hold risks and November hike – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Henry Cook expects the Bank of England to deliver a hawkish hold, with UK inflation driven higher by energy and headline CPI projected to exceed 4% after the January price cap reset.

item.title: Euro: Markets test ECB reaction function – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Senior Macro Strategist Bas van Geffen notes that EUR money markets now discount more than four additional European Central Bank (ECB) rate hikes beyond the two already delivered, as investors push expectations ahead of policymakers.
